title: A quasi-compact open of a base change descends to a finitely generated subalgebra
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over a field k, a k-algebra A and a quasi-compact open V of X_A, the lemma produces a finitely generated k-subalgebra A' of A and a quasi-compact open V' of X_{A'} whose base change to A is V (statement lines 811-820). The proof is an explicit descent through standard opens: choose finitely many affine opens U_i of X covering V, write each as the spectrum of a ring R_i, express V as a finite union of standard opens D(f_{ij}) inside the base changed charts, and then observe that finitely many elements of the rings R_i tensor_k A are involved, so a single finitely generated subalgebra A' contains all of them (proof lines 822-835). Setting V' to the union of the corresponding standard opens of X_{A'} gives the descent, and the equality V = pi^{-1}(V') is checked pointwise using that the f_{ij}' map to the f_{ij} (proof lines 836-841). The claim is H2: a finite-presentation bookkeeping argument carried out concretely, with the pointwise verification written out.
